title: Goal-Aware Identification and Rectification of Misinformation in Multi-Agent Systems
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.00509 (v1; only version per export.arxiv.org abs)
evidence: ARGUS: corrective LLM agent rectifies messages on critical channels (localized by edge-betweenness + embedding similarity). Only 3 fixed attacks (PI, RP, TI); no section on attacks aware of ARGUS. TSR reported under attack only; overhead only acknowledged qualitatively ('introduces computational overhead') in Limitations.

title: Monitoring Decomposition Attacks with Lightweight Sequential Monitors
bench: own:decomposition-attack dataset (QA, text-to-image, agent tasks; agent part adapted from AgentHarm)
evidence: Sec 3.3 'Adversaries Can Inject Random Tasks To Avoid Detections': 'adversaries can easily inject random tasks to mask their malicious intents further to avoid detections' (F1 0.85->0.72 at 100% injection) = hand-designed monitor evasion; no optimized attack. Prompted LLM monitor over cumulative user prompt history C_i=[p1..pi], 'flag and halt'. AgentHarm only seed (36 tasks adapted + 533 generated). F1/recall only, FP not reported separately. n_models = 5 monitor LLMs in main table.

title: Building a Foundational Guardrail for General Agentic Systems via Synthetic Data
evidence: Safiron (Ministral-8B, SFT+GRPO) + adapter judges planned trajectory pre-execution (input: env description, tool info, user query, planned actions; no tool outputs); outputs harmless/risky + risk category + explanation. No evaluation of plans crafted to fool the guard. Offline classifier only (no agent utility). fpr via harmful-detection precision 0.973 (FPR not separately stated). Threat model mentions malicious actors + 'External adversarial attack' risk category.

title: Breaking and Fixing Defenses Against Control Flow Hijacking in Multi-Agent Systems
bench: own:CFH-Hard (10 coding, 6 computer-use); AgentDojo (Slack, adapted to MAS, AutoGen Magentic-One)
evidence: ControlValve: CFG + contextual rules generated at planning 'before any untrusted content is ingested'; runtime deterministic CFG-edge check plus 'an LLM judge inspects the conversation trace' for contextual rules; outcomes 'permit, reject, or re-plan'. CFH attacks are adaptive vs. prior defenses (LlamaFirewall alignment check) but CV only tested with same attacks (0% ASR); no attack designed against CV. Main: o4-mini orchestrator + GPT-4o subagents; CV generator ablation o4-mini/GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini. Latency 128s vs 51s base. Over-restriction discussed qualitatively (App. D), not quantified.

title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
evidence: Monitor red-teaming: monitor-aware agents with hand-crafted evasion 'Monitor Hijacking', 'Lying with Jailbreaking Strategies', 'CoT Obfuscation' (prompted, not optimized). 'we focus on offline monitoring: the monitor inspects the complete agent trajectory' -> suspicion score only (decisions '-'). Monitor LLM Claude 3.6 Sonnet (agents: Claude 3.6 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 4 Sonnet). TPR@FPR=0.01 and AUC; hierarchical ~67x more efficient. HUMAN = targeted escalation to human overseers (+~15% TPR), review burden not measured.

title: Searching for Privacy Risks in LLM Agents via Simulation
bench: own:multi-agent privacy simulation (norms sampled from PrivacyLens; Training-5/Testing-100)
evidence: Search 'alternates between improving attack and defense strategies'; attack-search phase optimizes attacker instructions via simulation against the (fixed) defended data-sender agent -> defense in optimization loop. Defense = optimized system instructions (identity-verification state machine, consent from data subject) for the agent itself. Helpful action rate 93.4% -> 88.5%/31.2% (recovered to 94.5%/96.2% with helpful prompt). Transfer to 5 more models. Consent-asking frequency not systematically measured (Table 6 'consent-required holding' ratios unclear). arxiv_v1 not retrievable (abs page metadata not returned).

title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
evidence: Non-adversarial threat model: enforcing 'safety guard requests' (access control, safety rules) on target agent; no attack. Guard LLM generates task plan + guardrail code from human-written guard requests and target agent input/output logs; code execution yields label (access/action denied). Label precision/recall (LPP 100%, LPR 97.5% GPT-4 EICU-AC); FRA 100%; time 31.9s vs 8.5s. Core LLMs GPT-4, Llama3-70B, Llama3.1-70B, Llama3.3-70B.

title: Cowpox: Towards the Immunity of VLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
bench: own:VLM multi-agent album/RAG simulation (infectious jailbreak setting; AdvBench harmful targets); LLaVA-Bench (utility)
evidence: Sec 5.5 adaptive: 'attacker is aware of the strategies of COWPOX. He is also able to obtain the cure sample... attacker continues the optimization on the cure sample in order to achieve a higher RAG score than the cure sample' -> optimization against defense output. LLM inspector (output analysis module) flags infected answers; Cowpox agents replace virus with cure in album (memory). Inspector ACC 84.7%/89.1%, FNR reported, no FPR. Backbones LLaVA-1.5-7B (+InstructBLIP heterogeneous).

title: ShieldAgent: Shielding Agents via Verifiable Safety Policy Reasoning
evidence: Fixed attacks (e.g., AgentPoison, AdvWeb) only; no attack aware of ShieldAgent. Rules extracted offline by GPT-4o from human-written policy documents (regulations, handbooks) into probabilistic rule circuits; weights learned via hinge loss -> MIX. LLM shielding plan over action trajectory + history; binary safety label per action. FPR 4.8%; API queries -64.7%, inference time -58.2%; policy compliance conditioned on task success (ST-WebAgentBench). GPT-4o only.

title: On the Resilience of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration with Faulty Agents
bench: own:AutoTransform/AutoInject faults on HumanEval; CIAR; CommonMT; FairEval
evidence: Defenses Challenger (agents prompted to challenge received messages, reply 'unsafe'/'safe'; disposition of 'unsafe' not specified) and Inspector (extra LLM agent: 'decide whether the response below contain deliberate errors, If so, rewrite'). No faulty agents aware of or optimized against defenses. Defense results with GPT-3.5 only; w/o-errors performance reported (76.2 -> 76.8) but no FPR; no cost reported.

title: MELON: Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents
evidence: No adaptive attack: only 4 AgentDojo attack templates (Direct, Ignore Previous, System Message, Important Messages); limitation noted only for response-based attacks ('MELON only monitors tool calls, such attacks can evade detection'). Masked re-execution by the same agent LLM over tool outputs, tool-call embedding similarity threshold -> terminate. FPR 9.28%; 'masking run effectively doubles the number of required model calls'. GPT-4o, o3-mini, Llama-3.3-70B. VWA-Adv tried but excluded.

title: AdvEvo-MARL: Shaping Internalized Safety through Adversarial Co-Evolution in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
bench: NetSafe; AutoInject; own:UserHijack (chain/tree/complete topologies); utility: AIME24/25, LiveCodeBench, GPQA-diamond
evidence: Co-evolved RL attacker used in training only; test ASR uses fixed 'three widely adopted attack strategies' (NetSafe, AutoInject, UserHijack) 'applied to the trained defenders'; no attack optimized against final defenders. Safety internalized into task agents via MARL (Qwen2.5-3B/7B). ASR <20% vs baselines up to 38.33%; utility up to +3.67%. No over-refusal or overhead numbers. arxiv_v1 from Hugging Face 'Published on Oct 2, 2025' (abs submission history not retrievable).

title: AutoRAS: Learning Robust Agentic Systems with Primitive Representations
bench: own:Brain/Memory/Tool/Agent-to-Agent attacks on MMLU, MS-MARCO, MATH, ProgramDev; AgentHarm and ASB attack variants (App. A.4)
evidence: Attacks applied to randomly selected half of agents; 'stronger attack variants from AgentHarm and Agent Security Bench (ASB), both unseen during training' (not defense-aware); no attack optimized against the learned system. GFlowNet policy composes LLM-prompted safety primitives (SAFE_Filter remove injected instructions, SAFE_ToolGuard 'validate planned tool calls; if unsafe ... revise or reselect', SAFE_Trajectory, SAFE_CrossAgent). Total cost $0.6655 reported; no FPR/latency. arxiv_v1 date from pith.science record.

title: When Agents Go Rogue: Activation-Based Detection of Malicious Behaviors in Multi-Agent Systems
bench: own:stealthy prompt injection on CSQA, GSM8K; InjecAgent (tool manipulation); PoisonRAG; own:memory poisoning on HotPotQA
evidence: Limitation: 'Adaptive attacks that attempt to gradually shift activation distributions remain an open challenge'; none evaluated. AcMAS: cosine distance of agent activations to benign prototype (threshold) flags per-agent step before propagation; restorative activation steering and regeneration. FPR 0.04-0.07, AUROC 98.5-99.5; TCR 0.98; steering 185.3ms (12.4%). Backbones GPT-OSS-20B, DeepSeek-V3, LLaMA3-8B, Qwen3-30B-A3B.
